title: Hostility
intro: Shaytan wants to put hostility between people – Muslims answer with good words and brotherly love.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) tells the Prophet (SAW) to tell His servants to say only the best words, because Shaytan tries to stir up hostility between them. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Isra 17:53)</small>

Allah (SWT) made the Muslims a community of the middle way that calls to the right path and reminds others. Because of this role and this task from Allah, Muslims face constant attacks and hostility, because Shaytan’s plan is to harm those who try to live by Islam.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: In Surah Al-Ma’idah, ayah 91, Allah tells us that Shaytan wants to stir up hostility and hatred between you through alcohol and gambling, and to keep you from remembering Allah and from prayer. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Ma’idah 5:91)</small>

Hostility is a negative relationship between two or more people or groups. Someone who has hostility in their heart tries to put others down and shame them in front of people, to show that they are better.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) sets the relationship between Muslims with this ayah: the believing men and women are friends and protectors of one another. <small>(Qur’an, At-Tawbah 9:71)</small>

This relationship should be full of mercy, care, patience and support. In His wisdom Allah made Muslims brothers and sisters to each other – the love we have for our closest family is the model for how we treat our brothers and sisters in faith.

Hostility towards each other is a mark of those who turned against Allah’s laws, and Allah (SWT) will leave them in that state until they change. Muslims, however, know about Shaytan’s attacks – and also about the attacks of those who do not wish them well.

A much more dangerous problem is hostility and unrest that some Muslims bring into their own community (jama‘ah). Allah (SWT) says that persecution and strife (fitnah) are worse than killing. (Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:191)
Many problems in a community come from weak or unclear communication and misunderstanding, which make relations between people in the jama‘ah even worse.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Muslims are good and noble to those who are good to them. They don’t show hostility to anyone, and they are firm only with those who deserve it. They respect other people’s views and beliefs, but they defend and protect their faith and their brotherly love.

items.text: Saying the best words, even when you disagree
Asking calmly what someone meant before getting angry
Helping a brother or sister in the jama‘ah
Shaming someone in front of others to look better
Spreading a rumour at the masjid
Posting an angry comment without checking the facts

options: A negative relationship between people or groups

questions.q: Who wants to stir up hostility between people?
What should the relationship between Muslims be full of?
Where do many problems in a community come from?
How do Muslims treat other people’s beliefs?
options: They respect them, but protect their own faith

practice.title: Questions and talking with your teacher
prompts: 💬 What is the cause of hostility towards Muslims?
🤝 How should Muslims treat other Muslims, and how should they treat non-Muslims?
⚠️ Which kind of hostility is the most dangerous?
🗣️ Talk with your teacher about the saying (often linked to Sun Tzu): “Keep your friends close, and your enemies even closer.” What could it mean?
